sentences.text: Specimens of Bobbodus schaefferi include partial upper and lower teeth, the palatoquadrate, and the gill arch.
The genus Bobbodus was described by Zangerl in 1981.
The type species, Bobbodus schaefferi, is known from three specimens found on the ancient eastern coast of the Panthalassic Ocean.
Fossils of Bobbodus schaefferi have been found in the Kasimovian of Iowa, the Gzhelian of Nebraska, and the Asselian of Kansas.
Bobbodus is an extinct genus of eugeneodont holocephalians that lived during the Carboniferous and Permian periods.
Bobbodus belongs to the family Eugeneodontidae.
Bobbodus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Bobbodus lived from the Kasimovian to the Wuchiapingian stages, between 307 and 254.14 million years ago.
